# Results -- Study 539 (Cash-Flow-Volatility) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: form trailing
cash-flow volatility per name (std of quarterly operating cash flow / total assets), sort
cross-sectionally, go LONG the low-CF-vol tercile and SHORT the high-CF-vol tercile
(the Huang 2009 quality-like sign), equal-weight, one execution-lag day, measure monthly
returns on a large-cap survivor basket. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 2010 days × 40 tickers | `6385498e2186` |
| CF-vol signal (per ticker) | 40 tickers × 3 cols | `9f5b76cfb791` |
| Period covered | 2018-01-02 -- 2025-12-30 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close prices (auto_adjust=True) plus per-ticker
quarterly operating cash flow and total assets from `Ticker.quarterly_cashflow` /
`quarterly_balance_sheet`. Universe: 40 large-cap names across sectors.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is large-cap names *still trading in
2026*. Firms whose operating cash flows blew up and that subsequently delisted -- the
natural high-CF-vol short candidates -- are absent. All results are **upper-bound** estimates.

**Fundamental-data limitation (named explicitly):** yfinance serves only ~5 quarters of
cash-flow statements per name, so the CF-volatility characteristic is estimated on a thin,
recent history (it is a single stale cross-sectional snapshot, not a rolling re-formed
signal). A clean Huang (2009) replication needs Compustat-grade quarterly history; this is
a yfinance-feasibility test, and we let the verdict fall where it honestly falls.

## Synthetic positive control (faithful-engine / power check ONLY)

Averaged over **20 seeds** per planted premium (Welch-style), the long-short recovers a
planted CF-vol premium and returns noise under the null:

| Planted premium | Mean LS (%/yr) | Avg HAC t | Frac. \|t\|>=2 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | +0.20 | +0.11 | 0.15 |
| 0.04 | +8.14 | +4.51 | 0.95 |
| 0.08 | +16.08 | +8.90 | 1.00 |

The engine is faithful: ~zero at the null, monotone and significant when a premium is
planted. **This control is never cited to support the real-tape stamp.**

## The honest test -- real long-short

LONG low-CF-vol tercile (13 names), SHORT high-CF-vol tercile (13 names), equal-weight,
held over the price window with one execution-lag day.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N months | 95 (2018-02 -- 2025-12) |
| Mean return (annualised) | **-3.43%/yr** |
| Vol (annualised) | 9.81%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.350 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-1.027** |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 43.2% |
| Max drawdown | -34.7% |

- The long-short earns **-3.43%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-1.027** -- not merely below the
  |*t*| >= 2 bar, but with the **wrong sign**: the high-CF-vol leg *out*-performed the
  low-CF-vol leg on this survivor basket. The Huang (2009) anomaly does **not** reproduce here.
- Low-CF-vol leg: **+15.24%/yr**. High-CF-vol leg: **+18.67%/yr**. SPY: +14.25%/yr.
  High-CF-vol large-caps (e.g. NVDA, KO, JPM by this measure) led the 2018-2025 tape.

## Placebo / label-shuffle null (1000 permutations)

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real mean LS (monthly) | -0.286%/mo |
| Null mean / std | -0.015% / 0.301% |
| **Permutation p-value (two-sided)** | **0.357** |

The real long-short sits comfortably inside the shuffled-label null. There is no signal to
distinguish from random tercile assignment.

## Costs (10 bps one-way × turnover + 100 bps/yr borrow on short leg)

| Quantity | Gross | Net |
|---|--:|--:|
| Mean return (ann) | -3.43%/yr | -4.61%/yr |
| HAC t-stat | -1.027 | -1.381 |

Cost drag ≈ 1.18%/yr (15%/mo two-sided rebalancing turnover + short borrow). Costs only
deepen the loss; there is no gross premium for them to erode.

## Robustness -- split-fraction sensitivity

| Split | k per leg | Mean (%/yr) | HAC t | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Quintile | 8 | -4.56 | -0.85 | -0.33 |
| Tercile | 13 | -3.43 | -1.03 | -0.35 |
| Half | 20 | -0.87 | -0.26 | -0.09 |

Every split is negative and insignificant; the result is robustly **None** (not a knife-edge
of one cut). The execution-lag choice (1 vs 5 days) leaves the headline unchanged.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** HAC *t* = -1.027 on 95 months, placebo *p* = 0.357, and the sign is
  *reversed* vs Huang (2009). The cash-flow-uncertainty premium does not reproduce on this
  40-name large-cap survivor basket with yfinance's thin (~5-quarter) fundamentals. Robust
  across quintile/tercile/half splits. Literature support alone never lifts a verdict to
  Weak/Real on this desk -- the real tape decides, and it is silent.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Negative gross (-3.43%/yr) and negative net (-4.61%/yr),
  Sharpe -0.35, max drawdown -34.7%. There is no gross edge; costs and short borrow only
  make it worse. Nothing to trade.
- **Huang (2009) direction -- BUSTED (on this tape).** The anomaly says low CF-vol earns
  *higher* returns; here the high-CF-vol leg won (+18.67% vs +15.24%/yr). On survivors with
  a thin signal window, the effect is absent and the sign flips -- the on-brand outcome for
  a pointed academic factor replicated honestly on a small survivor basket.
